solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Century with hoary bite? Time to wrap up

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a snap is a quick bite, as a dog makes

explanation.surface: An old frosty nip in the air signals it is time to bundle up warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the cheeky reading of 'bite' as the nip of the cold itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spell of chilly weather is exactly when people put on coats and scarves.

clue.text: Constant projections for rises

parts.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
arms and legs project from the body

explanation.surface: Ledges sticking out give a steady supply of footholds for ascents.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbs and rises are both verbs for going up, as roads or prices do.

clue.text: Keen Latin historian displaying Spanish article

indicators.note: a word displaying another holds it out on show within itself

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic Roman writer shows off a Spanish text.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and lively both describe someone eager and full of energy.

clue.text: Pavements in Wales kids found unsettling

indicators.note: unsettling means disturbing from a settled arrangement

explanation.surface: Welsh children feel uneasy walking on the paved streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidewalk is the American word for the British pavement beside a road.

clue.text: A short article by poet about nothing applying to all

indicators.note: about means surrounding, placed round the outside

explanation.surface: A brief piece by a poet concerning nothing in particular has universal relevance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A short article' reads as one phrase; split it as A + short (cross) + article.
explanation.definitionFit: Across-the-board describes measures that cover everyone or every case equally.

clue.text: Public funds bashes around end of August

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it inside

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: final letter of the month name

explanation.surface: Government money takes a beating as summer draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks are government securities, a form of public borrowing held by investors.

clue.text: Jog round a deck

explanation.surface: A runner does a lap around a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship, but it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a pack of cards used in fortune-telling, and a deck is a pack.

clue.text: Fellow author to dominate ceremony, right

explanation.surface: A fellow writer tries to take over a ceremony, rightly so.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-writer is a partner who shares the authorship of a work.

clue.text: Rays causing problems (note, European answer is included)

indicators.note: something included is put inside a larger piece

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means note well

explanation.surface: Some rays cause trouble, an aside notes about a European reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the reader's NB rather than a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbeams are shafts or rays of light from the sun.

clue.text: Dodgy character stole motor that's out of place?

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so not in proper order

explanation.surface: A shady figure stole a car that looked out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a wealthy London district; the phrase mocks off-road vehicles used only for city school runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea tractor is a big four-wheel-drive SUV, out of place on smooth urban streets.

clue.text: Drive carelessly with an aggressive sort, say

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters fall out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A road-rage motorist drives recklessly, being a hostile type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' reads as an instruction to a motorist but is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is one example of a hostile, attacking person, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Strong currency is got through effort

parts.note: the won is the currency of Korea

explanation.surface: A sturdy currency is earned only by hard graft.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard-won was achieved only after great struggle and exertion.

clue.text: Live cattle's sound downstairs

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Mooing from living cattle drifts up from the floor beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstairs means on a lower floor, so the adverb below can replace it.

clue.text: Game's solution, it nearly was displayed

indicators.note: nearly means not quite whole, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: in chemistry a sol is a colloidal solution
a programme that was displayed on air was aired

explanation.surface: Someone almost revealed the answer to a puzzle game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' looks like the answer to the game but is the chemist's sol; only 'was displayed' loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a one-player card or peg game, also called patience.

clue.text: Fool blooming cremated what goes with scones

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person

indicators.note: blooming as a mild oath, read as letters bursting out in a new form

explanation.surface: A fool exclaims about something being cremated, which is morbid for teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' tempts as a dessert definition, which fits the scones; it is just the clot.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick clotted cream is the traditional partner of scones in a British cream tea.

clue.text: Chicken and fish — the bane of some kitchens

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Chicken and fish are staples that cooks may come to hate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockroaches are pests that infest kitchens, eating scraps and spreading dirt.

clue.text: Busy bee and plain commoner

indicators.note: busy suggests constant bustling movement, jumbling the order

explanation.surface: A worker bee is industrious, simple and ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebeian was a member of the common people of ancient Rome, and now any ordinary person.

clue.text: Southern mother's hot tan is an overwhelming triumph

parts.note: ma is mother, here with the possessive
H for hot, as on taps
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A southern mum's deep suntan is a great success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tan' looks like sunburn but is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a hugely successful show, song or film.

clue.text: Leaves battle with muscle wrenched

indicators.note: wrenched means twisted violently out of shape

explanation.surface: A fighter quits the battle after pulling a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb of departure but is the noun for salad greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb's lettuce is a small salad plant eaten for its tender green leaves.

clue.text: Northbound salesperson found in coach — fantastic

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading from bottom to top
one thing found in another lies inside it

parts.note: a coach is a type of bus
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman heading north on a coach finds it wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb and fantastic are both terms of high praise for excellent things.

clue.text: Best and also worst

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to best someone is to get the better of them
second meaning: to worst someone is likewise to beat them

explanation.walkthrough: Best and worst look like opposite adjectives, but both are verbs meaning the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, both best and worst mean to overcome or beat an opponent.

clue.text: Gaffer, a star gaining in brilliance, provides dance music

parts.note: a gaffer is a boss or foreman
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A manager and his star player bring rhythm to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossa nova is a Brazilian style of music and dance blending samba and jazz.

clue.text: Vote to cut leader's portion

indicators.note: cutting the leader means removing the opening letter

explanation.surface: A vote to reduce the party leader's share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portion' is the verb here, to share out.
explanation.definitionFit: To portion out and to allot both mean to distribute shares.

clue.text: Ruddy rapscallion shifting last of swag

indicators.note: shifting means moving to a different spot in the word

parts.note: adds no letters: it names which letter of the rascal moves, the final letter of swag

explanation.surface: A red-faced crook moves the tail end of his loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the G, which is the last of 'swag', shifts one place to the right in the rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is French for red and also a red cosmetic, matching ruddy colouring.

clue.text: One person's close and comparatively in the pink with this decongestant

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, its last letter

parts.note: in the pink means hale, healthy; the comparative is haler

explanation.surface: Someone feels nearer to good health thanks to this cold remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With this' points the wordplay at the device itself, which is what the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler delivers medicine by breath, and some are used to clear a blocked nose.

clue.text: Gin to calm, as you'd say, swingers' bar?

indicators.note: as you'd say points to the way words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a gin is a trap for game; to calm is to ease

explanation.surface: A drink to settle the nerves at a bar for swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin is a snare, not the spirit, and the bar is a crossbar, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from ropes on which acrobats swing.

clue.text: Record an absence of art gallery?

parts.note: no expresses that something is absent
the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: A question of whether a town lacks any gallery to show art.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to write down or set in writing, as one records music.

clue.text: Rule out expert greeting bishop with it

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A specialist forbids a church official from joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit is to forbid, ruling out by order something that might happen.
